title: Finiteness of a finite type ring map descends along a directed colimit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ a directed system of commutative rings (ring maps $A_i\to A_{i'}$ for $i\le i'$, compatible), with colimit $A=\varinjlim_iA_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $0\in I$, let $B_0$ and $C_0$ be commutative $A_0$-algebras and $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$ a homomorphism of $A_0$-algebras which is of finite type ($C_0$ is generated as a $B_0$-algebra, via $\varphi_0$, by finitely many elements). For $i\ge0$ regard $A_i$ as an $A_0$-algebra via the transition map, and $A$ via the coprojection, and put $B_i=A_i\otimes_{A_0}B_0$, $C_i=A_i\otimes_{A_0}C_0$, $\varphi_i=\mathrm{id}_{A_i}\otimes\varphi_0:B_i\to C_i$, and $B=A\otimes_{A_0}B_0$, $C=A\otimes_{A_0}C_0$, $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\varphi_0:B\to C$. If $\varphi$ is finite ($C$ is a finitely generated $B$-module via $\varphi$), then there is an $i\ge0$ such that $\varphi_i$ is finite ($C_i$ is a finitely generated $B_i$-module via $\varphi_i$) (Stacks Algebra, Lemma 07RG).

source.place: Lemma Tag 07RG (lemma-colimit-finite, line 47522) and its proof (generators $x_1,\dots,x_m$ of $C_0$ over $B_0$, monic polynomials $P_j$ over $A\otimes_{A_0}B_0$ killing $1\otimes x_j$, lifted to a finite stage)

proof.text: *Step 2 (monic equations over $A$).* By hypothesis $C$ is a finitely generated $B$-module via $\varphi$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] (with the ring map $\varphi:B\to C$) every element of $C$ is integral over $B$; in particular for each $j=1,\dots,m$ there are $d_j\ge1$ (after multiplying the monic polynomial by $T$ if its degree is $0$) and $b_{j0},\dots,b_{j,d_j-1}\in B$ with $P_j(1\otimes x_j)=0$ in $C$, where $P_j=T^{d_j}+\sum_{k<d_j}b_{jk}T^k\in B[T]$ and $P_j(y)$ means $y^{d_j}+\sum_k\varphi(b_{jk})y^k$. (Stacks: 'Pick monic polynomials $P_j\in A\otimes_{A_0}B_0[T]$ such that $P_j(1\otimes x_j)=0$ in $A\otimes_{A_0}C_0$'.)

*Step 3 (the coefficients come from a stage).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise] part (1) with $M_0=B_0$ (an $A_0$-module; then $M_i=B_i$, $M=B$, $\mu_i=\beta_i$, $\mu_{i'i}=\beta_{i'i}$): each of the finitely many coefficients $b_{jk}$ is $\beta_{i_{jk}}(b'_{jk})$ for some $i_{jk}\ge0$ and $b'_{jk}\in B_{i_{jk}}$. As $I$ is directed, choose $i\ge0$ with $i\ge i_{jk}$ for all $j,k$, and replace $b'_{jk}$ by $\beta_{i\,i_{jk}}(b'_{jk})\in B_i$, which still maps to $b_{jk}$ (step 1, $\beta_i\beta_{i\,i_{jk}}=\beta_{i_{jk}}$). Put $P_{j,i}=T^{d_j}+\sum_kb'_{jk}T^k\in B_i[T]$, monic, mapping to $P_j$ coefficientwise. (Stacks: 'For some $i\ge0$ we can find $P_{j,i}\in A_i\otimes_{A_0}B_0[T]$ mapping to $P_j$'.)

*Step 4 (the equations hold at a later stage).* With $i$ and $P_{j,i}$ from step 3 let $z_j=(1\otimes x_j)^{d_j}+\sum_k\varphi_i(b'_{jk})(1\otimes x_j)^k\in C_i$. As $\gamma_i$ is a ring map with $\gamma_i(1\otimes x_j)=1\otimes x_j$ and $\gamma_i\varphi_i=\varphi\beta_i$ (step 1), $\gamma_i(z_j)=(1\otimes x_j)^{d_j}+\sum_k\varphi(b_{jk})(1\otimes x_j)^k=P_j(1\otimes x_j)=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise] part (2) with $M_0=C_0$ ($M_i=C_i$, $\mu_i=\gamma_i$, $\mu_{i'i}=\gamma_{i'i}$): for each $j$ there is $i_j\ge i$ with $\gamma_{i_j i}(z_j)=0$; take $i'\ge i_1,\dots,i_m$ (directedness), so $\gamma_{i'i}(z_j)=\gamma_{i'i_j}\gamma_{i_ji}(z_j)=0$ for all $j$. Put $b''_{jk}=\beta_{i'i}(b'_{jk})\in B_{i'}$; since $\gamma_{i'i}$ is a ring map fixing $1\otimes x_j$ and $\gamma_{i'i}\varphi_i=\varphi_{i'}\beta_{i'i}$, $0=\gamma_{i'i}(z_j)=(1\otimes x_j)^{d_j}+\sum_k\varphi_{i'}(b''_{jk})(1\otimes x_j)^k$ in $C_{i'}$. So each $1\otimes x_j\in C_{i'}$ is a root of the monic polynomial $T^{d_j}+\sum_kb''_{jk}T^k\in B_{i'}[T]$, i.e. integral over $B_{i'}$ via $\varphi_{i'}$. (Stacks: 'Since $\otimes$ commutes with colimits we see that $P_{j,i}(1\otimes x_j)$ is zero in $A_i\otimes_{A_0}C_0$ after possibly increasing $i$'.)

*Step 5 (conclusion).* At the index $i'$ of step 4, $C_{i'}$ is generated as a $B_{i'}$-algebra via $\varphi_{i'}$ by $1\otimes x_1,\dots,1\otimes x_m$ (step 1 with $T=A_{i'}$), each integral over $B_{i'}$ (step 4). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] (with $R=B_{i'}$, the ring map $\varphi_{i'}$, $B=C_{i'}$, $b_j=1\otimes x_j$), $C_{i'}$ is a finitely generated $B_{i'}$-module, i.e. $\varphi_{i'}$ is finite. (Stacks: 'Then this $i$ works.')
